description: Binds one component property to live datasource data instead of a static value: the Property's own Type flips from "Value" to "Variable" and gains a VariableRef child. Silently inert unless the ref is ALSO registered in the page's own Page::VariableRef list.
notes: THE gotcha (cost a full failed render before being solved): a VariableRef node can exist, be fully wired to its Container and Property, and STILL render nothing until its id is also added to the page-level Page::VariableRef list. Registered-but-orphaned vs orphaned-but-unregistered look identical everywhere except that one list — captured directly from a before/after fix pair where the only diff was this registration.

The VariableRef is registered in THREE places at once: Page::VariableRef (page-wide registry — the one that silently gates rendering), Container::VariableRef (its immediate host), and Property::VariableRef (the specific property whose value it overrides). All three plus the VariableRef's own Page/Container/Property scalar back-pointers must agree.

Type:"DatasourceParameter" with Variable dot-paths like "item.<field>" is the form used inside a Repeater template (each row's own data) — see widget_repeater.json. A ref reading a page-level Variable's own fields instead (e.g. "selectedRecord.sample_id_field") is the same node shape by convention but was not directly captured with that exact dot-path root; do not assume the LHSType/Type string carries over unchanged without confirming.

Once bound, the Property's Type is "Variable" and its "Value" key is dropped entirely — leaving a stale Value alongside Type:"Variable" was never observed and should not be written; the two are mutually exclusive on every capture seen.
